messages.subject: Announce: Workshops, St Andrews, Summer 2006
parts:
Dear distance-sampling list:

This is a preliminary announcement of the workshops we're planning for St
Andrews, Summer 2006. Details are not finalized yet, but the dates and
approximate course contents are set, as outlined below, and also on our web
site
http://www.creem.st-and.ac.uk/conferences.php

We expect to open registration for all three workshops early in 2006.
Meawhile, if you wish to express interest in attending, please email the
workshop organizer, Rhona Rodger at rh...@mcs.st-and.ac.uk

Cheers,

- Len Thomas

Distance Sampling Workshops: St Andrews 2006

Workshop 1: Introduction to Distance Sampling
23 August 2006 - 25 August 2005
A three-day introductory workshop, focusing on standard distance sampling
methods. It is a blend of theory and practice,and participants will learn
how to use the industry-standard program Distance. Participants will gain a
solid grounding in both survey design and methods of analysis for distance
sampling surveys.

Workshop 2: Advanced Techniques and Recent Developments in Distance Sampling
28 August 2005 - 30 August 2005
A 2.5 day workshop designed for those who are already familiar with the
basics, where we will teach advanced material such as automated survey
design, adaptive sampling, incorporating covariates into the detection
function and methods for where g(0)<1. Participants will learn the more
advanced features of Distance. Note that this workshop is natually
complemented by the subsequent workshop on density surface modelling.

Workshop 3: Primer on Density Surface Modelling from Distance Sampling Data
31 August 2006 - 01 September 2006
This two day short course will focus upon methods of predicting abundance or
density of biological data using the count method of Hedley and Buckland
(2004, Chapter 4 of Advanced Distance Sampling). Variation in animal
density/abundance is modelled as functions of covariates such as land cover
type, habitat, bathymetry, altitude or depth. General additive models (GAMs)
or general linear models (GLMs) will be fitted to estimated densities along
transects using a new analytical engine inside program Distance. This is an
advanced workshop for those already familiar with distance sampling.
Participants intending to model their own data will be required to have it
formatted according to precise specifications prior to arrival at St.
Andrews.
